title: Conductor onramp tiles — priority presets & inline tuning snapshots
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a compact set of onboarding tiles (the 'Conductor' mini-flow) that surface recommended presets and inline tuning snapshots for the Optimize toolkit. Each tile should map to a priority preset (Low-Latency, Cost-Efficient, Balanced) and expand to show a 1-2 line rationale plus concrete configuration suggestions: batching strategy, KV cache TTL/prefixing hints, and quantization profile (e.g., fp16, int8, int4). Goal is to help first-time users pick safe defaults and to provide a quick path to advanced settings. Deliver responsive assets for console header, quickstart modal, and the in-product Optimize panel.
goals: Reduce time-to-first-meaningful-inference for new Optimize users
Provide clear, actionable defaults so users don’t guess batch/cache/quant settings
Make tuning recommendations scannable on a single card with an optional expanded snapshot
Create handoff-ready assets for engineering: annotated frames, spacing tokens, and copy variants
deliverables: 3 compact tile designs (collapsed) + 3 expanded snapshots with recommended params
Microcopy variants for each priority preset (short, medium, long)
A/B copy variants for CTA: 'Apply preset' vs 'Preview settings'
Figma file with developer tokens and export-ready PNG/SVGs
Accessibility notes (contrast, keyboard interactions) and pixel-spec PDF
Handoff ticket(s) to ENG with implementation notes and example API payloads
acceptance_criteria: Figma frames include annotated token names and spacing scales
Each preset lists batching recommendation (mode + target batch size), KV cache guidance (ttl/scope), and quantization profile
Copy approved by PM and content reviewer
Dev tickets created and linked (ENG-40211 for panel, ENG-40212 for modal)
Assets exported at 2x and provided as PNG + SVG with correct naming
QA checklist written for localization + accessibility
tasks: Kickoff workshop with PM & runtime engineer to define safe default ranges
Design expanded snapshot layout with inline code-style hints for payload examples
Write microcopy variants and tooltips for each parameter
Run internal readability test (5 engineers) and iterate
Prep handoff package and create ENG implementation tickets
engineering_notes: Preferred interaction: collapsed tile shows icon + short rationale; click expands inline without modal
Backend: provide /recommendation API returning {preset, batch_hint, kv_ttl_ms, quant_profile} for preview
Need example payloads for low-latency vs cost-efficient to include in snapshot
Consider telemetry hooks: track which preset applied and whether users open advanced panel
review_feedback: Noah Rivera (PM): emphasize safety — presets must never degrade model correctness beyond acceptable threshold
Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): suggest adding 'compatibility' badge when a preset relies on a quantized runtime
UX Research (Marta Lopez): prefer 'Preview settings' default CTA; users want to see exact batch sizes
Content (Ravi Kapoor): shorten Low-Latency microcopy and avoid jargon in first-pass variant
decisions: Use three presets only for MVP: Low-Latency, Cost-Efficient, Balanced
Expanded snapshot will include an inline JSON example, truncated to 2 lines with 'view more' link
Tile interaction uses slide-down expansion (no modal) to reduce context switches
